source_quote: Medically necessary for home use for gastric suction due to inability to empty gastric secretions through normal gastrointestinal functions.

criteria.description: Inability to empty gastric secretions through normal gastrointestinal functions

review_notes: Home model suction pump indicated for severe dysmotility or obstruction.

policy_title: Clinical Policy CP.MP.107: Durable Medical Equipment and Orthotics and Prosthetics Guidelines (Rev. 08/26)
source_quote: Medically necessary when meeting both of the following: A. One of the following indications: 1. Chemotherapy for liver cancer: primary hepatocellular carcinoma or Duke’s Class D colorectal cancer, in which the metastases are limited to the liver and where either the disease is unresectable, or the patient refuses excision of the tumor; 2. Anti-spasmodic drugs for severe spasticity: administered intrathecally to treat chronic intractable spasticity in member/enrollee unresponsive to less invasive medical therapy including both of the following: a. A 6-week trial of noninvasive methods, such as oral anti- spasmodic drugs, that failed to adequately control the spasticity or produced intolerable side effects; b. Prior to pump implantation, there has been a favorable response to a trial of intrathecal dose of the anti-spasmodic drug; 3. Other uses when all of the following are met: a. The drug is reasonable and necessary for the treatment of the individual; b. It is medically necessary that the drug be administered by an implanted infusion pump. The infusion pump has been
clinical_service_or_procedure: Implantable infusion pumps (HCPCS E0782, E0783, E0785, E0786)

criteria.description: Liver cancer chemo (Duke's Class D / unresectable), severe spasticity with failed 6-wk oral trial and successful intrathecal trial, or other FDA-approved use

required_documentation: Oncology or physiatry notes confirming diagnosis
Documentation of 6-week oral trial failure and successful intrathecal trial (for spasticity)
FDA approval status for drug and pump indication
dependencies: CP.MP.173 for chronic intractable pain opioid pumps
review_notes: For opioid pumps for intractable pain, refer to CP.MP.173.

policy_title: Clinical Policy CP.MP.107: Durable Medical Equipment and Orthotics and Prosthetics Guidelines (Rev. 08/26)
source_quote: B. None of the following contraindications to implantation of an infusion pump: 1. Known allergy or hypersensitivity to the drug being used (e.g., oral baclofen, morphine, etc.); 2. Active infection; 3. Body size insufficient to support the weight and bulk of the device; 4. Presence of another implanted programmable device; 5. Heparin or insulin is the drug intended for administration.

criteria.description: Known allergy or hypersensitivity to drug being used
Body size insufficient to support weight and bulk of device
Presence of another implanted programmable device
Heparin or insulin is drug intended for administration

review_notes: Absolute contraindications including heparin/insulin pump administration.

policy_title: Clinical Policy CP.MP.107: Durable Medical Equipment and Orthotics and Prosthetics Guidelines (Rev. 08/26)

policy_title: Clinical Policy CP.MP.107: Durable Medical Equipment and Orthotics and Prosthetics Guidelines (Rev. 08/26)
source_quote: Medically necessary when used as a monitoring and alarm device for any of the following: A. To monitor individuals on a home ventilator or with a tracheostomy B. To determine appropriate home oxygen requirements C. To wean an individual from home oxygen D. To monitor an unstable respiratory condition

required_documentation: Pulmonology clinical documentation of ventilator, tracheostomy, oxygen weaning, or unstable condition
review_notes: Covered as a continuous monitoring/alarm device for qualifying indications.

policy_title: Clinical Policy CP.MP.107: Durable Medical Equipment and Orthotics and Prosthetics Guidelines (Rev. 08/26)
source_quote: Not medically necessary when used for any of the following: A. Oximetry when used as a diagnostic procedure B. Monitoring of a stable respiratory condition C. Asthma management D. Other conditions not listed above
review_notes: Explicitly non-covered for routine asthma, stable conditions, or diagnostic testing.
